newsitem.title: USA: Stockpile cobalt sales policy may change - lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Stockpile cobalt sales policy may change - lawyer.

text.p: The way U.S. Stockpile sells cobalt in sealed bid solicitations may change following the court ruling, due next Tuesday, on a complaint filed by trader Minor Metal Inc, a lawyer for the company said.
At a hearing in the U.S. Court of Federal Claims, Judge Tidwell said a written decision on the case would be issued May 20.
But David Dempsey of Piper & Marbury, acting for Minor Metals, said he understood that Judge Tidwell was likely to order some changes in Stockpile sales policy.

Minor Metals' complaint to the Court of Federal Claims alleged Stockpile acted against the law in its March sealed bid offering by prohibiting an "all or none" clause, using a "Best Value" criteria for awarding metal when price alone should be the determinant, and including a domestic preference evaluation.
Dempsey said Judge Tidwell appeared likely to rule that the "all or none" clause was valid in sealed bid negotiations.
"In the Best Value issue, the government conceded that three weeks ago, saying they were not going to press it," Dempsey said.
But Dempsey understood Judge Tidwell may disallow a domestic bidder, in a sealed bid solicitation, to match the price of a bidder who intended to export any metal bought from Stockpile.
Stockpile attorneys said earlier they would not comment on the case until Judge Tidwell's written ruling on all three complaints to the Court of Federal Claims was made known next week.
Stockpile cobalt sales have been suspended since March, and this, according to some dealers, has helped push up prices.
